questions.question:
**Direction: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks and make the sentence meaningful.**

The _______ from my window is of the ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** ‘scene; sea.’**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• The sentence implies that there is a sea outside the window. One can see the sea from the window.
 
• From the given sentence it is clear that both the blanks will be filled in by nouns.
 
• **Seen and see** are verbs.
 
• We can easily eliminate the options.
 
• Only option (3) consists of two nouns **‘scene’ **and **‘sea.’**
 
• **Scene** (दृश्य): a specific view or setting. (एक विशिष्ट दृश्य या सेटिंग)
 
 
• **Example**: *The sunset created a breathtaking **scene**__ over the mountains.*
 
 
 
• **Sea **(समुंदर): a large body of saltwater; ocean. (खारे पानी का एक बड़ा भंडार; महासागर)
 __
 
• **Example**: *The **sea**__ was calm and beautiful on a sunny day.*
 
 
 
• Hence, **‘scene’ and ‘sea’ **will be the most appropriate to fill the blanks.
 
• The correct answer is **option 3.**

**Correct sentence**: *The __**scene**__ from my window is of the __**sea**__.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **See** (देखना): is a verb that means to perceive something with the eyes, to observe or witness.

 
 
• **Example**: I can see a beautiful rainbow in the sky.
 
 
 
• (Scene and Seen), (See and Sea) are Homonyms.
 
• **Homonym: **Same sound but different meaning.

questions.question:
**Direction: Select the correct option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select ‘No substitution.’**

They **__is going__** to Delhi with their friends.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"are going."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the Subject-Verb agreement, a singular subject takes a singular verb and a plural subject takes a plural verb.
 
• The subject **"they"** is a plural pronoun and it requires a plural verb.
 
 
• **Example**: ***They are**__ leaving the house.*
 
 
 
• **"Are going"** is a plural verb.
 
• The correct answer is **Option 4.**

**Correct sentence**: *They __**are going**__ to Delhi with their friends.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• "Was going" is incorrect because it uses a singular verb for a plural subject.
 
• "Will going" is incorrect because it uses "will" and "going" together, which is redundant.

• **For Example -** *After a week-long vacation on the beach, he returned to work feeling refreshed and **renewed**__.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Could"** is the correct option to fill in the blank number 3.
 
• **"Could"** is a modal verb that indicates possibility or ability.
 
 
• **Example**: *She **could**__ sell me those flowers.*
 
 
 
• In this context, using **"could"** implies that the action is possible but not guaranteed.
 
• The correct answer is option 1.
 
• Correct passage:

A beautiful spectacle for anyone to __behold__ would be the crowds that throng to see the Indian cricket team playing, whether it be in India or in other parts of the globe. This __undoubtedly__ is the occasion where the spirit of oneness is all pervasive. India with all its diversity __**could**__ be seen either rejoicing or moaning depending on the sway of the game ______ (4) ______ watched. Unity in diversity is ______ (5) ______ in all its glory.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2, "shouldn't", **would imply that the action is not advisable or recommended.
 
• **Option 3, "won't",** would imply that the action is impossible or unlikely to happen.
 
• **Option 4, "shan't", **is an outdated contraction of "shall not" and is not commonly used in modern English.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"witnessed."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The verb **'witnessed'** means to see or observe something happening. (किसी चीज़ को घटित होते हुए देखना या निरीक्षण करना)

 
 
• **Example**:* "I **witnessed**__ the accident on the highway yesterday."*
 
 
 
• It is the most appropriate option to fill in the blank, as it fits the context of the sentence.
 
• The correct answer is option 3.
 
• Correct passage:

A beautiful spectacle for anyone to __behold__ would be the crowds that throng to see the Indian cricket team playing, whether it be in India or in other parts of the globe. This __undoubtedly__ is the occasion where the spirit of oneness is all pervasive. India with all its diversity __could__ be seen either rejoicing or moaning depending on the sway of the game __being__ watched. Unity in diversity is __**witnessed**__ in all its glory.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Option 1, redressed**: means to correct or remedy a problem. (सही करना, सुधार करना, ठीक करना)

 
 
• **Example**: *"The company **redressed**__ the customer's complaint by offering a refund."*
 
 
 
• **Option 2, terraced**: means to create a series of flat areas on a hillside. (किसी पहाड़ी पर समतल क्षेत्रों की श्रृंखला बनाना)
 __
 
• **Example**: *"The farmers **terraced**__ the land to prevent soil erosion."*
 
 
 
• **Option 4, procured**: means to obtain something through effort or action. (प्रयास या क्रिया द्वारा कुछ प्राप्त करना)
 __
 
• **Example**: *"The manager **procured**__ a new printer for the office."*
